paper_sections.title: Replication experiment with a different set of famous faces

description.value: High-resolution fMRI study using ROI-based univariate and multivoxel pattern analyses to examine decoding of famous face identities in temporo-frontal face-selective and adjacent non-face-selective regions.

spans.text: In the current high-resolution functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging study, we systematically examined the decoding of the identity of famous faces in the temporo-frontal network of face-selective and adjacent non-face-selective regions.

description.value: Observational repeated-measures neuroimaging study of healthy volunteers performing a block-designed one-back task during multiple fMRI sessions, with independent functional localization and identity-decoding analyses.

spans.text: The stimuli were presented in blocks (block-design).

In the current high-resolution functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging study, we systematically examined the decoding of the identity of famous faces in the temporo-frontal network of face-selective and adjacent non-face-selective regions.
MRI data were collected using a 3T GE MRI scanner with an 8-channel head coil.

description.value: Functional scans were realigned, motion corrected, normalized to 2 × 2 × 2 mm voxel resolution using an MNI template, and spatially smoothed.

spans.text: The functional scans were realigned, motion corrected, normalized to 2x2x2 voxel resolution using MNI template and smoothed with a FWHM = 3 mm kernel.
SPM5 (Wellcome Trust Centre for Neuroimaging, London, UK;   http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk  ) was used for data analysis.
The normalization was done using unified segmentation procedure [ 44 ].
smoothed with a FWHM = 3 mm kernel

description.value: For multivoxel pattern analysis, data were detrended, z-score normalized separately for each session, shifted by two TRs to account for hemodynamic lag, and global signal was subtracted separately for each condition.
